meaning:
τρέμω
to tremble, esp. with fear: Mrk.5:33, Luk.8:47; with ptcp. (in cl more frequently with inf.), 2Pe.2:10.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had been done to her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
When the woman saw that she was not hidden, she came trembling, and falling down before him declared to him in the presence of all the people the reason why…
but chiefly those who walk after the flesh in the lust of defilement and despise authority. Daring, self-willed, they are not afraid to speak evil of…
